sessionabstract:
In today’s connected world, protecting your digital identity is essential—both professionally and personally. This engaging session provides faculty and staff with practical, easy-to-apply strategies to stay safe online. Participants will learn how to recognize common threats such as phishing, social engineering, and ransomware, and understand how these risks impact higher education environments.

The training will cover best practices for securing accounts (including password management and multi-factor authentication), safeguarding sensitive data, and using institutional systems responsibly. We’ll also explore how to maintain privacy on personal devices, navigate social media safely, and avoid common online scams.

Designed for all skill levels, this session emphasizes real-world scenarios and actionable tips you can use immediately. Attendees will leave with increased awareness, confidence, and the tools needed to protect themselves, their colleagues, and their institution from evolving cyber threats.

Foregrounding Care: Recognizing Moments of Activation and Utilizing Self-Regulation Strategies
sessionabstract: We are all managing a lot these days, both in our work and in our personal lives, and it is easy to feel overwhelmed. The implications of this show up in many ways in the classroom and workplace. Our students often struggle with executive functioning, are experiencing increasing levels of anxiety, and are coping with depression that can, at times, feel incapacitating. Our colleagues are navigating competing demands on their time, and feeling overextended can be emotionally taxing in ways that can cause both tension and conflict. This session will invite us to explore moments when the behaviors we are observing—or experiencing ourselves—are the result of feeling activated. We will consider the impact of these moments, for the individual feeling activated, for those present in the classroom or workplace, and for our roles as educators, advisors, coaches, colleagues, or supervisors. This session will offer concrete strategies that can be used both during moments when individuals are feeling activated and as regular practices that help support self-regulation.

Faculty & Staff Guide to Reciprocal Wellness - Supporting Our Students, Supporting Ourselves
sessionabstract: Introduction: who we are; where to find us; when students should be referred for counseling; the referral process; steps to engaging in counseling; confidentiality; cost and resources available to students. The aim of our counseling center is to support students with mental health concerns. The goal of this presentation is to look at wellness as reciprocal. How well you do in supporting your students is affected by how well you are doing. We will look at the importance of recognizing the interconnection between cultivating wellness in our students and in ourselves. By paying closer attention to shifts in your baseline you will be better attuned to students who are struggling. Self-awareness is the first step to better self-care. Noticing the early signs that you are stressed or overwhelmed can help you intervene before things become unmanageable. We will help you identify what leads you to feeling overwhelmed and stressed and what helps you to feel calm and relaxed. Self-care doesn't have to be relegated to the end of the workday. We will look at how you can integrate better self-care into your workday to support yourself and your students.

sessionTitle: "Be the Professor You Needed": Intentional Course Design for Empathy & Care
sessionabstract:
What does it actually mean to create a classroom where students feel safe enough to learn? Not the compliance version — the accessibility statement buried in your syllabus, the land acknowledgment you read once — but the kind of care that shapes how you design every policy, every assignment, every interaction from day one.

This workshop invites faculty to reflect on what empathetic teaching looks like in practice: building structures where students don't have to "trauma dump" to get an extension, where showing up matters more than performing, and where your policies say I am on your team before a student ever has to ask. We'll explore practical strategies for humanizing your classroom — from syllabus language to day-one framing — grounded in the belief that education should be dignity-affirming and psychologically safe for everyone in the room, including you.

Leave with language, examples, and a framework you can use this semester.

sessionSpeakers: AnnaMaria Omilanowicz, River Vooris, and Kyrstin White
sessionabstract: The Multicultural Life and Diversity Office staff will facilitate a workshop talking about informal and formal mentoring relationships between students and colleagues. We will discuss the benefits of mentoring, personal experiences, and best practices. Participants will explore how meaningful mentoring relationships can support personal growth, academic success, career development, and a sense of belonging. Through this workshop attendees will learn strategies for building authentic connections and examine ways to navigate challenges that may arise within mentoring relationships. The workshop will also highlight the importance of building relationships with and creating supportive environments for individuals from diverse backgrounds. Whether participants are currently serving as mentors, seeking mentorship, or interested in developing stronger professional and personal relationships, this session will provide practical tools and insights to foster impactful mentoring experiences that contribute to individual success and community building.

sessionabstract:
Join your librarians for a relaxed, crafty mixer to discover how the library can support your classes while having fun with creative activities sponsored by the Makerspace. Come for the origami; stay for the friendly librarians!

Librarians partner with faculty to teach information and AI literacy classes, create tailored digital resources like assignment specific webpages and Brightspace modules, and provide research help for your students in a variety of accessible formats.

Come to chat, make, or ask questions. As a bonus, learn how bad some of us are at crafting! We’re here to make your work a little easier and a lot more connected.

In this session, you’ll get an overview of the features of YuJa, our all in one video platform, and see how it will transform your classroom experience.

We’ll start with an overview of the platform, including how YuJa video storage works and how your media is organized. Next, you’ll explore video creation on both the web platform and the mobile app. From there, you’ll explore ways to edit your videos. We’ll then walk through YuJa’s two types of video quizzes and demonstrate how each integrates seamlessly with your Brightspace gradebook.

To wrap up, you’ll get a first look at YuJa Panorama—our new accessibility tool that will eventually replace Ally.

Questions are encouraged throughout the presentation, so bring your curiosity and ideas!
